title: Wedding Guest Outfit Peace Treaty
oneLiner: A playful dress-code translator that helps couples and guests avoid Pinterest costume wars, budget shame, and awkward declines.
targetUser: Wedding couples, guests, planners, family coordinators, and wedding-party members negotiating confusing dress codes, color palettes, travel budgets, and social expectations.
keyUX: Paste a dress-code line or outfit concern, translate it into plain guest-friendly expectations, compare "wear what you own" options, and generate a tactful couple/guest message that protects both photos and relationships.
sourceSignals: S9 - Reddit r/weddingplanning, guest attire requirements backlash, May 29 2026
S10 - Reddit r/weddingplanning, dress-code clarity vs anxiety, Mar 2026
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive playful web app prototype called "Wedding Guest Outfit Peace Treaty" for wedding couples, guests, planners, and family coordinators dealing with confusing or overly strict dress codes. The app should let a user paste invite wording or describe an outfit concern, translate the dress code into plain expectations, check guest budget and closet reality, compare acceptable outfit options, and generate tactful clarification or pushback scripts. Required sections: dress-code drama meter, invite wording translator, guest budget and closet reality check, outfit acceptability lane, couple expectation dial, tactful pushback and clarification scripts, photo-palette compromise board, and shareable peace treaty card. Use realistic wedding sample data with travel cost, gift cost, color palette, "cocktail" confusion, and one hyper-specific attire request. Design direction: use the `playful-experimental` profile with bold social-game energy, expressive but readable cards, bright contrast accents, humorous status labels, and polished shareable artifacts that feel like a portfolio-worthy wedding diplomacy toy.
